items.title: Integral Witt classes and rational Seifert isometric structures

references.title: Charles Livingston, A Survey of Classical Knot Concordance
Charles Livingston and Allison N. Miller, The concordance genus of knots, II
Neal W. Stoltzfus, Algebraic Computations of the Integral Concordance and Double Null Concordance Group of Knots

items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice when an integral Seifert lattice comes from a knot's positive-push pairing. For an integral Seifert lattice $(H,V)$, its integral Witt class is its class in $G_{\mathbb Z}$ from the definition of metabolic Seifert form and algebraic knot concordance. An isomorphism $(W,B,T)\to(W',B',T')$ of rational isometric structures is a rational-linear bijection $P:W\to W'$ such that $B'(Px,Py)=B(x,y)$ and $PT=T'P$. A rational isometric structure is a triple $(W,B,T)$ in which $W$ is a finite-dimensional even-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-vector space, $B:W\times W\to\mathbb Q$ is a nonsingular symmetric bilinear form, $T:W\to W$ is an invertible linear map satisfying $B(Tx,Ty)=B(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in W$, and $I-T$ is invertible. Such a structure is metabolic if it has a $T$-invariant subspace $L\subset W$ with $\dim_{\mathbb Q}L=\frac12\dim_{\mathbb Q}W$ and $B|_{L\times L}=0$. Define the rational Witt group $G_{\mathbb Q}$ by direct sum of isomorphism classes, with metabolic structures set equal to zero. For a nonsingular integral Seifert matrix $V$, the associated matrix pair is $(B,T)=(V+V^T,V^{-1}V^T)$; whether this pair is a rational isometric structure is established separately.

The definition concerns finite-rank bilinear forms and isometry data. It does not identify the unrelated Witt Lie algebra with either $G_{\mathbb Z}$ or $G_{\mathbb Q}$.

items.title: Every integral Seifert form is realized by a knot

references.title: Charles Livingston, A Survey of Classical Knot Concordance
Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links

items.statement: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $g\geq0$ and let $V\in M_{2g}(\mathbb Z)$ satisfy $\det(V-V^T)=\pm1$, where the empty skew matrix has determinant $1$. There is a connected compact smooth oriented surface $F\subset S^3$ with one boundary component and an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ whose positive-push Seifert matrix is exactly $V$.

items.title: The negative Seifert form represents the algebraic inverse

references.title: Charles Livingston, A Survey of Classical Knot Concordance

items.statement: Assume full AC when the form is obtained from a knot. For every integral Seifert lattice $(H,V)$, the class represented by $(H,-V)$ is the additive inverse of the class represented by $(H,V)$ in $G_{\mathbb Z}$.

items.title: A positive Hopf plumbing gives the trefoil Seifert matrix

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links
Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes

items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. A positive Hopf band is an oriented annulus whose two boundary components, with their induced orientations, have linking number $+1$. Let $F$ be the genus-one Seifert surface obtained by plumbing two positive Hopf bands in a square, with oriented core curves $a,b$ forming a positive handle basis, and choose the plumbing side so that $a^+$ bounds a disk in $S^3$ disjoint from $b$. The oriented boundary of this standard positive two-band plumbing is the right-handed trefoil. In the positive-push convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ with ordered basis $(a,b)$, the Seifert matrix is
$$
V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

items.title: An elementary Seifert enlargement preserves the algebraic concordance class

references.title: W. B. Raymond Lickorish, An Introduction to Knot Theory
references.locator: Chapter 8, Theorem 8.2, printed pp. 79–81; full text used for the enlargement convention

references.title: Charles Livingston, A Survey of Classical Knot Concordance

items.statement: Assume full AC for any knot-derived Seifert matrix. Let $V$ be an integral Seifert matrix and let $E_0(V;x,y,z)$ or $E_1(V;x,y,z)$ be either elementary enlargement in the definition of S-equivalence, where $x,y\in\mathbb Z^{2g}$ and $z\in\mathbb Z$. Then $E_0(V;x,y,z)$ and $E_1(V;x,y,z)$ are integral Seifert lattices, and each represents the same element of $G_{\mathbb Z}$ as $V$.

items.title: An invertible Seifert matrix gives a rational isometric structure

references.title: Charles Livingston and Allison N. Miller, The concordance genus of knots, II
Charles Livingston, A Survey of Classical Knot Concordance

items.statement: Assume full AC for the knot Seifert-pairing convention. Let $V\in M_{2g}(\mathbb Z)$ be an invertible Seifert matrix and put $B=V+V^T$ and $T=V^{-1}V^T$ on $\mathbb Q^{2g}$. Then $B$ is a nonsingular symmetric bilinear form, $T$ is an invertible $B$-isometry, and $I-T$ is invertible; hence $(\mathbb Q^{2g},B,T)$ is a rational Seifert isometric structure.

items.title: Classification of rational and integral algebraic concordance

references.title: Charles Livingston, A Survey of Classical Knot Concordance

references.title: Neal W. Stoltzfus, Unraveling the Integral Knot Concordance Group

references.title: Charles Livingston and Allison N. Miller, The concordance genus of knots, II

items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice for knot Seifert pairings. Let $G_{\mathbb Q}$ be the rational Witt group of finite-dimensional even-dimensional nonsingular symmetric rational forms equipped with an invertible isometry $T$ for which $I-T$ is invertible, modulo metabolic $T$-invariant subspaces, and let $G_{\mathbb Z}$ be the integral algebraic concordance group of Seifert lattices. The rational algebraic concordance classification due to Levine and the integral classification completed by Stoltzfus identify each of these abelian groups, as an abstract group, with
$$
\mathbb Z^{(\mathbb N)}\oplus(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^{(\mathbb N)}\oplus(\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z)^{(\mathbb N)}.
$$
Here $A^{(\mathbb N)}$ denotes the direct sum of countably infinitely many copies of the abelian group $A$; the statement does not identify Levine's rational classification with the distinct integral group or claim that their defining objects are the same.

items.title: The algebraic concordance map is a surjective homomorphism

references.title: Charles Livingston, A Survey of Classical Knot Concordance
references.locator: §2.2, Theorems 2.8–2.9 and complete proof of Theorem 2.9, printed pp. 323–324

references.title: Arunima Ray, Slice Knots and Knot Concordance
references.locator: Course II, §3, Definitions 3.1/3.5 and Proposition 3.6, printed II–11–II–12; explicit topological algebraic-concordance map on II–12; external TOP group-law input

items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}}$ and $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}}$ denote, respectively, the smooth and locally flat topological concordance groups of smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, with connected sum as operation. Let $G_{\mathbb Z}$ be the integral algebraic concordance group generated by integral Seifert lattices modulo direct-sum and metabolic relations. In either category $\mathcal C$, the rule $[K]\mapsto[(H_1(F;\mathbb Z),V_F)]$, where $F$ is any connected oriented Seifert surface of $K$ and $V_F$ is its positive-push Seifert pairing, defines a surjective group homomorphism $\Phi_{\mathcal C}:\mathcal C\to G_{\mathbb Z}$.

title: Algebraic concordance and metabolic forms — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Worked cases for metabolic Seifert forms

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links
references.locator: §8.A, printed pp. 200–202; trefoil Seifert matrix example

references.title: Charles Livingston, A Survey of Classical Knot Concordance

items.statement: Assume full AC. The disk Seifert surface of the oriented unknot has the rank-zero Seifert lattice and is metabolic. In the positive-push convention, the standard positive Hopf-band plumbing for the right-handed trefoil has matrix $V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Since $V$ is invertible, its rational isometric structure has symmetric form $B=V+V^T=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-1\\-1&-2\end{pmatrix}$, which is negative definite; the integral Seifert lattice is not metabolic.

items.title: Unimodular skew part does not force metabolicity

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links
references.locator: §8.A, printed pp. 200–202; trefoil Seifert matrix example

references.title: Charles Livingston, A Survey of Classical Knot Concordance

items.statement: Assume full AC. The false claim is: every positive-rank integral Seifert lattice with unimodular alternating part is metabolic. The right-handed trefoil's positive-push Seifert lattice has $V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ and $V-V^T=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$. Its invertible matrix gives the rational isometric structure with $B=V+V^T=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-1\\-1&-2\end{pmatrix}$, which is negative definite; the rational extension of $V$ has no isotropic line, so the rational-to-integral saturation lemma has no input. No rank-one integral subgroup has zero Seifert self-pairing, so the lattice is not metabolic.
